wavy-cap.habitat: Woodchip and bark mulch in parks, flower beds, landscaped car parks and gardens; also rich woody debris. Introduced; mainly in towns
wavy-cap.summary: Brown mushroom with a strongly wavy cap edge, growing in clusters on woodchip mulch, bruising blue. A Class A drug, and deadly Galerina grows on wood too.

banded-mottlegill.name: Banded mottlegill
banded-mottlegill.habitat: Manured or composted ground: dung heaps, stable bedding, compost, well-manured fields and gardens
banded-mottlegill.summary: Brown mushroom on manured ground whose cap dries paler from the centre, leaving a dark band at the edge. Contains psilocybin (Class A).

spectacular-rustgill.name: Spectacular rustgill
spectacular-rustgill.habitat: Large clumps at the base of broadleaf trees (often oak) and on stumps and buried roots; sometimes conifers
spectacular-rustgill.summary: Big golden-orange mushroom in clumps at tree bases, with a ring and rusty-orange spores. Intensely bitter and poisonous.

pholiotina-rugosa.name: Deadly conecap
pholiotina-rugosa.habitat: Woodchip and bark mulch, flower beds, lawns, gardens, compost and disturbed rich soil; also grassland and woodland edges
pholiotina-rugosa.summary: Tiny, fragile orange-brown mushroom with a membranous ring, common in garden mulch and lawns. Contains amatoxins, the death cap poison.

thorn-apple.name: Thorn-apple
thorn-apple.season: Flowers Jul–Oct; spiny seed pods Aug–Nov
thorn-apple.habitat: Casual on disturbed ground: arable fields, waste ground, gardens, tips and under bird feeders (from birdseed); commonest in hot summers in southern and eastern England
thorn-apple.summary: Rank-smelling weed with large white trumpet flowers pointing upwards and spiny, walnut-sized seed pods. Every part is deadly poisonous.

henbane.name: Henbane
henbane.habitat: Disturbed sandy or chalky ground: coastal sand and shingle, farmyards, field edges, old rabbit warrens, waste ground; scarce and scattered, mainly in England
henbane.summary: Sticky-hairy, foul-smelling plant with dull creamy-yellow flowers netted with purple veins. Contains the same deadly alkaloids as deadly nightshade.

mandrake.name: Mandrake
mandrake.season: Flowers in spring (autumn mandrake Sep–Nov); yellow-orange fruits follow
mandrake.habitat: Not wild in the UK. Grown in some gardens, herb gardens and botanic collections; native to the Mediterranean
mandrake.summary: Low rosette of large crinkled leaves with purple or pale bell flowers and yellow tomato-like fruits. Garden plant only in the UK; poisonous throughout.

angels-trumpet.name: Angel's trumpet
angels-trumpet.season: Flowers Jun–Oct outdoors; much of the year under glass
angels-trumpet.habitat: Gardens, patios, pots and conservatories; not frost-hardy, so never wild in the UK. Often stood outside in summer
angels-trumpet.summary: Garden shrub with huge, hanging, scented trumpet flowers in white, yellow, pink or peach. Every part is deadly poisonous.

wormwood.name: Wormwood
wormwood.habitat: Waste ground, roadsides, old gardens, quarries and coastal rough ground; scattered, mainly England
wormwood.summary: Silvery-grey, intensely bitter, aromatic perennial with finely divided leaves and small drooping yellow flower heads. Contains thujone, which can cause fits.

nutmeg.name: Nutmeg
nutmeg.season: All year (kitchen spice; the tree grows only in the tropics)
nutmeg.habitat: Kitchen cupboards, food stores and ration packs; not grown in the UK
nutmeg.summary: Common kitchen spice that is safe in cooking but causes poisoning when large amounts are eaten, by children or deliberately. Symptoms are delayed.

opium-poppy.name: Opium poppy
opium-poppy.habitat: Gardens, allotments, waste ground, tips, roadsides and field edges (a common garden escape); also licensed farm crops in southern England
opium-poppy.summary: Tall blue-grey poppy with large white, pink, mauve or red flowers and a big round seed head. Its sap and seed heads contain opioids such as morphine.

ergot.name: Ergot
ergot.season: Jul–Sep, in the ears of ripening grasses and cereals
ergot.habitat: Rye, wheat, barley and many wild grasses, including field edges, verges and coastal grasses; commonest after a wet flowering season
ergot.summary: Hard, dark purple-black, horn-like growths replacing grains in grass and cereal ears. Poisonous: ergotism caused gangrene, fits and hallucinations in the past.

cannabis.name: Cannabis
cannabis.habitat: Occasional casual on waste ground, tips, roadsides and under bird feeders (from birdseed); licensed low-THC hemp crops in fields
cannabis.summary: Tall, strong-smelling plant with hand-shaped leaves of narrow, saw-edged leaflets. Class B drug; identification only.
